**Authorization and checks.** The billing page’s `Page` in [`settings/billing/page.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/settings/billing/page.tsx) passes plan selections to `changePlanAction`. `BillingPlanCard` in [`billing-plan-card.tsx`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/components/domain/billing/billing-plan-card.tsx) disables plan changes for anyone who fails `can(actor, "org:manage_billing", ...)`. The [`ROLE_MATRIX`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/lib/permissions.ts) requires the `owner` role for that action; platform staff also bypass the role check.

When submitted, `withAction` validates the request against `changePlanSchema` and resolves the actor. The handler in [`change-plan.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/actions/billing/change-plan.ts) checks billing permission, then `assertPlanFitsCurrentUsage` compares current seat, project, and storage usage with the **target plan’s** limits from `getPlanLimits`. It calls `wouldExceedLimit(targetPlan, resource, used, 0)`, so usage is allowed right up to the limit and rejected only when it is over. `BillingService.changePlan` in [`billing-service.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/server/services/billing-service.ts) repeats the scope and permission checks and checks seats, projects, storage, and webhook endpoint count against the target plan. Neither gate checks `issuesPerProject`.

**Persistence and follow-up.** If those checks pass, `changePlan` calls `subscriptionRepo.updateSubscriptionPlan`. In [`subscription-repository.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts), that updates `subscriptions.plan`, the interval, and status to `active`. The billing page’s selection handler always submits `"monthly"`. The update does **not** change `organizations.plan`. `planFor` in `billing-service.ts` treats `subscriptions.plan` as authoritative when a subscription exists, falling back to `organizations.plan` only if there is no subscription.

After saving, `changePlan` emits `billing.plan_changed` with the old and new plans. The listeners registered by `registerEventHandlers` from [`instrumentation.ts`](/private/tmp/luna-scratch-20261008/2b0ebb61-f98b-4ad7-a832-fa2162f3e47f/src/instrumentation.ts) record an activity entry through `ActivityService` and enqueue deliveries for configured webhook endpoints through `WebhookService`. The action also revalidates the billing and organization tags.

**What changes elsewhere—and what does not.** `BillingService.checkLimit` uses `planFor`, so its checks immediately reflect the new subscription plan. Those checks feed the dashboard layout’s seat and project meters, the Members page’s `SeatLimitBanner` and invite form, and the organization usage API. Some of those views also read `organizations.plan`: for example, the Members page’s seat-check data can show the lower allowance while its plan label still names the old plan.

Most product gates and write-side quota checks read `org.plan` directly, though. That includes project creation, invitations and invitation acceptance, issue creation, attachment storage, webhook creation and delivery, and archived-data retention. Feature-flag evaluation also gets its plan from `org.plan` via `buildFlagContext`; plan-gated features such as the activity feed, digest email, webhooks, advanced search, and public projects therefore continue using the old plan after this change. The billing usage panel reads the subscription plan, but the billing header and “Current” plan card marker use `org.plan` and can also remain stale. So the subscription’s new value does affect subscription-backed limit checks, but the organization’s denormalized plan value is not synchronized, leaving many non-billing product behaviors and displays on the former plan.
